_about: Per-comment hawk/dove labels for the dashboard, written by the scheduled labelling task. Keyed by item id from collect.py. score: +10 most hawkish to -10 most dovish, judged as likely market impact against current pricing. Optional brief fields (from 23 Oct 2026): sum = one bold sentence; pts = 2-6 key points; rr = rates read, what it means for pricing; ev = event/venue; basis = verbatim (read the bank's own text) or reports (news paraphrase only).

4cafd6da09f6.read: Less slack and sticky wages; wants to proactively lean against second-round effects.
4cafd6da09f6.sum: Greene said there is less labour-market slack than thought and the MPC should proactively lean against second-round effects of the energy shock.
pts: Said 'there is less slack than we thought' and it 'may have peaked'; unemployment fell from 5.2% to 4.7%.
Underlying pay growth about 3.4% (AWE) to 4.5% (RTI), plateauing 'closer to 3.5% than 3%', risks to the upside.
Expects inflation above 4% during the January–April 2027 pay round.
Household inflation expectations up to 4.5% short-term and 4.3% longer-term; firms' price expectations 3.7%.
Called the energy shock 'protracted'; said it is 'not obvious' policy is meaningfully restrictive.
'I continue to believe we should proactively lean against the risk of second-round effects.'
4cafd6da09f6.rr: Supports the November hike priced and argues against pricing early cuts in 2027; one of the more hawkish MPC voices.
